title: Recommendation Orchestrator: webhook-driven rollout and idempotent apply for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Add API and webhook primitives to Redwood Optimize to safely propose, apply, and roll back batching and caching configuration recommendations. This ticket covers the server-side endpoints, webhook event shapes, idempotent apply semantics, and the minimal SDK helpers required by internal automation jobs and early enterprise customers.

Background: Optimize currently generates recommendations (batch size, KV cache policies, quantization hints) stored in the console. Customers requested an automation path to apply recommended configs automatically or via CI. Prior work implemented suggestion CRUD and a prototype webhook for notifications (ENG-11805, ENG-9421). We need a production-ready contract with strong safety guarantees: idempotent ops, audit trail, safe rollback, and observable runbooks.

Proposal summary:
- Add /v1/optimize/recommendations POST to create a recommendation with a generated recommendation_id and optional client-provided idempotency_key.
- Add /v1/optimize/recommendations/{id}/apply POST to start a guarded apply. Apply accepts apply_mode (dry_run|canary|full), target_scope (model|route|customer), and optional rollout_policy (percentage, step_interval_seconds). Apply must be idempotent: repeated requests with same idempotency_key are no-ops after the first accepted apply result.
- Add /v1/optimize/applications/{application_id} GET to query status and /rollback POST to perform automated rollback to previous config snapshot.
- Webhook channel: emit events for recommendation.created, apply.started, apply.progress, apply.completed, apply.failed, apply.rolled_back. Each webhook payload includes recommendation_id, application_id, status, actor, timestamp, and a compact diff representing config delta. Delivery guarantees: at-least-once; consumers must handle duplicates.
- SDK helpers: convenience methods in Node and Python SDKs to create+apply with exponential retry, dedupe via idempotency key, and a switch to verify canary results before automatic ramp-up.

Safety and constraints:
- Apply operation must first perform a dry_run simulation against a replica control-plane to validate compatibility and performance delta estimate. If dry_run fails, apply should transition to failed and emit apply.failed with failure_reason.
- Canary mode: apply a recommendation to a constrained subset (default 5%) and monitor configured metrics (latency P95, error_rate, cost_per_token) for a configurable window. Automatic ramp occurs only if thresholds are met.
- Rollback must be automatic if critical thresholds are breached during canary or full rollout, and manual rollback must be available via API call. All config snapshots must be retained for 90 days and associated with application_id.

Security: API endpoints require Optimize write scope and a signed webhook secret for verification. All apply actions are recorded in the audit log with actor identity (service principal or human) and idempotency_key.

Deliverables: API spec, webhook event schema, server implementation (service + job orchestrator), SDK helper functions, end-to-end tests, canary runbook, dashboards for apply telemetry, docs for customers/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints implemented and integrated with existing Optimize store
Idempotency respected across retries and deduplicated by idempotency_key
Webhook events emitted for all apply lifecycle states and retriable by queue consumer
Dry_run simulation returns compatibility report before any state change
Canary mode performs metric checks and triggers automatic ramp or rollback
Rollback API restores previous runtime config and emits apply.rolled_back event
SDK helpers available for Node and Python with examples in docs
E2E tests for failure/retry/duplicate webhook handling added to CI
Audit log entries contain actor, idempotency_key, and snapshot id

rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal rollout to staging and a single canary customer (2 engineers) - enable dry_run and webhooks only. Phase 2: enable canary mode with 5% traffic gating and automated metrics checks for a beta cohort. Phase 3: GA with 50% default rollout and opt-in autopilot for customers. Rollout toggles controlled by feature flag optimize.apply.alpha and blocked by security review. Each phase gated by runbook drills and SRE sign-off.
api_contract_summary: Create recommendation returns 201 + recommendation_id; apply endpoint accepts idempotency_key and returns application_id synchronously when accepted (or 202 if queued). Use GET /applications/{id} for status. Rollback returns 200 with rollback_snapshot_id. Error codes: 400 invalid input, 409 precondition failed, 423 apply locked, 500 server error.
idempotency_strategy: Primary dedupe by client-provided idempotency_key stored with application record; server checks key + actor identity + target_scope before creating a new application. If a duplicate request arrives within retention window, return existing application_id and canonical status. All operations include deterministic operation IDs to allow replay diagnostics.
test_plan: Unit tests for handler logic, integration tests for dry_run simulation and canary monitor, chaos tests to simulate duplicate webhook deliveries, end-to-end test that exercises apply -> canary -> automatic ramp and rollback. Add CI job to run the canary simulation in staging on every merge to main.
monitoring: New dashboards: optimize.apply.latency, optimize.apply.failure_rate, optimize.apply.rollback_rate, canary.metric_violations. Alerting: PagerDuty on apply.failed with high customer_impact or if rollback occurs in >2% of applies in 24h. Track idempotency_key collision metrics for anomalous client behavior.
